_comment: THE MANAGER'S CHECKLIST. Every work item in the CURRENT manager session's
scope, and the state of each.
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE, 2026-09-01, verbatim in intent: 'every manager session
keeps a detailed checklist of work items in its scope (this may be updated
as work progresses and the workplan is adapted, eg an unforeseen blocker
that needs to be resolved to release the rest of the items) - and every
status update should start with the checklist, then summary of what has
been done (recently) and what's next.'
SO THE REPORTING CONTRACT IS FIXED: checklist -> recently done -> next.
In that order, every time. A status update that opens with a narrative is
not following this.
WHY IT LIVES IN THE REPO AND NOT IN A SESSION'S CONTEXT. Same reason as
MANAGER-LEASE.json and SESSIONS.json: it must survive its holder's DEATH
and be readable by a manager arriving COLD. A checklist held only in
context is lost exactly when a successor most needs it, and re-deriving it
costs the successor the hours that produced it.
IT IS ADAPTIVE, NOT A FROZEN PLAN. The directive is explicit that it
changes as work progresses -- an unforeseen blocker that must be resolved
to release the rest is a first-class edit, not a failure of planning. Add
the blocker as its own item, point the blocked items at it, and say so.
STATES ARE NEVER COLLAPSED. 'delegated' is not 'in progress' and neither is
'done'; 'blocked' names WHAT it waits on. Most importantly 'done' means
MERGED AND OBSERVED, while 'landed_unproven' means the code is in and its
effect has NOT been seen on the fleet -- the distinction this whole system
keeps paying for when it is skipped.
THE MANAGER DOES NOT EXECUTE THESE ITEMS. Operator-directed the same day:
'the manager session only manages and does not take even small items,
because that means they're not focused on what they're actually supposed
to be doing.' An item with owner 'manager' is a MANAGEMENT act (a merge, a
deploy, a lease heartbeat, a spawn), never a build.

states.landed_unproven: merged; effect NOT yet observed on the fleet
states.in_flight: a session is actively working it
states.blocked: waiting on a named thing; see blocked_on
states.queued: scoped and agreed, nobody started it

items.title: The ping duplicate IS real and measured; I archived the session fixing it and told the board it was not
items.note: ⚠️ THIS ROW PREVIOUSLY READ `dropped` WITH 'THE DEFECT WAS NEVER DEMONSTRATED'. THAT WAS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED. The session had already measured it from the live journals: 22:10:19.934 bridge drain tick STARTS, 22:10:21 trader-bot tick reads the SAME file and delivers it, 22:10:23.212 bridge POST returns and unlinks. Both drainers do read -> send -> unlink, so the file survives the whole POST; the bridge's POST took 3.28s against ~1ms on every other tick that day. The copies went to different BOTS because ict-telegram-bot started at 21:37:37Z, before the secret was set at 22:08:26Z, and _resolve_claude_bot() caches once per process. === WHERE MY REASONING FAILED: I read the operator's later 'nothing showed up in both feeds' as REFUTING the earlier 'sent to both channels'. It does not. The mechanism is INTERMITTENT BY CONSTRUCTION — a duplicate needs the winning drainer's POST to exceed the ~2s phase gap between two 5s ticks. Absence on later pings is what the mechanism PREDICTS. === AND THE DUPLICATE IS THE LESS SERIOUS HALF: when the race is won outright one copy is sent, but WHICH CHAT it lands in is decided by scheduler phase, and an operator cannot learn where to look for a channel picked at random. === #10695 reached the same mechanism independently and called it correctly ('predicts intermittent duplication rather than reliable doubling'). Two sessions, same finding, while I had told the board it was not real. === STATUS: #10694 is Tier-2 and stays DRAFT — it changes a live service's drain behaviour and needs ict-telegram-bot.service restarted after merge, which is an operator OK I do not have overnight. FIRST ITEM ON THE MORNING REPORT.

items.title: A superseded pending system-action run is cancelled with NO comment posted back
items.note: Found by the ping test (#10695) when P1b vanished. Three send-ping actions dispatched inside 15s and the MIDDLE run was cancelled: issue left open, zero comments, nothing anywhere saying the action never ran. `cancel-in-progress: false` protects a RUNNING job, but GitHub keeps only one PENDING run per concurrency group, so a third queued run cancels the second. ⚠️ THE ISSUE COMMENT IS THE ONLY RESULT SURFACE A PM-SIDE SESSION HAS, so 'silently dropped' is indistinguishable from 'still queued' — a session can wait forever on a run that is already dead. The test session's workaround was to dispatch strictly one at a time, which is exactly the sort of unwritten discipline that decays. Filed as BL-20260901-SYSTEM-ACTIONS-CANCELS-A-SUPERSEDED-PENDING-RUN-AND-COMMENTS-NOTHING-BACK-SO-A-DISPATCHED-ACTION-IS-SILENTLY-LOST.

items.title: The Data Explorer serves the live journal to anyone on the public Caddy host
items.blocked_on: operator — gating a live public read route is Tier-2 and would change what the Svelte SPA can render
items.note: ⚠️ TOP ITEM FOR THE MORNING REPORT, ABOVE THE RETIREMENT DECISIONS. Surfaced by session_01LvzsinECH8HP in #10687 and then MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MANAGER rather than taken on report — plain curl, no Authorization header, from outside the VM against https://ict-bot.duckdns.org : /api/bot/db/table/trades -> HTTP 200, total 5,318 · order_packages -> 200, 4,275 · balance_snapshots -> 200, 29,892. NEGATIVE CONTROL: device_tokens -> HTTP 404, so #10682's exclusion genuinely holds and the probe can distinguish a refusal from a serve. The filing session counted `signals` at 2,301,022 rows. === WHY IT HAPPENED, AND IT IS NOT A CODING ERROR: CLAUDE.md justifies the Data Explorer as Tier-1 on the premise 'no secrets in either DB' — a claim about CREDENTIALS, not about the CONFIDENTIALITY of the trading record. That judgement was made while the API sat on a firewalled IP reachable only server-side by Streamlit. Caddy was then added (2026-08-13) so the browser-direct Svelte SPA could reach the API over HTTPS, and NOBODY RE-DERIVED THE TIER DECISION AFTER THE TRANSPORT CHANGED. The route did not become less safe; the world became able to reach it. === HONEST SEVERITY, in the direction that does not overstate: this is a CONFIDENTIALITY exposure, NOT a control path. The explorer is SELECT-only on a mode=ro connection with bound values and schema-validated identifiers; nothing writes, no order can be placed, and no credential is reachable now that device_tokens is excluded. Nobody's money can be moved with it. What is exposed is the operator's complete trading record — every trade, order package and balance snapshot. === ⚠️ DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED TONIGHT, and that is a decision rather than an omission. Gating a live public read route is Tier-2, and the Data Explorer tab of the Svelte SPA reaches this route BROWSER-DIRECT, so adding a bearer would break a working operator surface. Doing that unannounced at 02:00 while the operator sleeps trades a three-week-old read exposure for a broken dashboard they wake up to. The options worth putting to them: leave it (the record is not secret), gate it behind DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN and teach the SPA to send one, or put Caddy basic-auth in front of /api/bot/db/* only. === ⚠️ THE BLAST RADIUS IS NOW BOUNDED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY REASONING — the manager probed the same public host unauthenticated for anything WRITEABLE or PRIVILEGED and every gate refused: POST /api/bot/prop/report (the one route that writes the journal) -> HTTP 401 'missing authorization', confirming its documented FAIL-CLOSED behaviour; GET /api/pnl -> 401 and GET /api/status -> 401, so require_session is genuinely enforced on both session-gated routes; GET /api/diag/version -> 401 without a bearer. SO: NO UNAUTHENTICATED WRITE EXISTS ANYWHERE on the public surface, and no privileged read. The exposure is exactly and only the Tier-1 READ surface. That is what makes 'confidentiality, not control' a measured statement rather than a hedge, and it is why this can wait for the operator rather than being fixed unilaterally overnight. === Incidental confirmation worth keeping: this independently verifies CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-13 correction that require_session enforcement IS live on /api/pnl and /api/status — an earlier version of that row said 'issuance only', which was stale in the dangerous direction. items.title: The standing 'scheduled workflows here never fire' assumption is FALSE, and the truth is worse-shaped
items.note: ⚠️ THIS CONTRADICTS A STANDING ASSUMPTION THAT IS QUOTED IN AT LEAST THREE PLACES — OI-20260901-SCHEDULED-PROBES-AND-DUE-LIST-HAVE-NEVER-FIRED-ON-CRON, the header comment of .github/workflows/work-digest.yml, and MI-03's own note — all of which tell a session that a correct cron here is not evidence it will run. MEASURED BY THE MANAGER 2026-09-02T01:50Z, repo-wide, event=schedule, n=30 completed runs: FIFTEEN DISTINCT WORKFLOWS FIRED ON CRON, 29 of 30 successful. Among them are probes AND due-list — the exact two the OI row says have never fired. === THE OI ROW'S OWN CLEARING CRITERION IS MET, and I ran the precise probe it specifies rather than a proxy: `actions_list` on probes.yml filtered to event=schedule returns total_count=1 — run #34, event `schedule` (NOT workflow_dispatch, which that row explicitly says does not count), conclusion success, created 2026-09-01T10:12:17Z on main. === ⚠️ BUT DO NOT SIMPLY CLEAR IT AND MOVE ON, BECAUSE THE REAL FINDING IS THE TIMING AND IT IS THE PART THAT AFFECTS THE OPERATOR. probes.yml declares `20 5 * * *` and fired at 10:12 — FOUR HOURS FIFTY-TWO MINUTES LATE. work-digest declares `20 2,6,10,14,18,22` (raised from `20 6`) and fired at 00:19, matching no slot. So the honest statement is NOT 'cron never fires' and NOT 'cron works' — it is CRON FIRES, HOURS LATE AND AT AN UNPREDICTABLE OFFSET. That is a THIRD state both existing claims collapse, and it is the one that matters for the 06:20 morning digest: the operator may get it mid-morning rather than on waking. === n=2 offsets is not a delay distribution and must not be quoted as one; what is established is that the offset is large and nonzero, not its size. ROUTE TO: session_01TASYv35o6XciFnMC9wmnHi, which is already investigating exactly this question and should own both the OI clearing and the corrected wording — clearing a monitoring row is an observation its clearer must have made, and that session will have the fuller picture including the 02:20Z slot.

The reporting bias survives (test_unattributable_is_preserved_and_still_reported, test_could_not_check_is_never_a_clean_pass, test_lower_bound_caveat_survives_on_every_reporting_render). ⚠️ landed_unproven with an UNUSUALLY CHEAP observation available: this manager opens a manager-only PR every sweep, and ten of those were flagged against my own branch. The very next one either stops reporting a self-match or does not. Watch the audit comment on the NEXT manager PR and record which. === ✅ OBSERVED WORKING 2026-09-02T04:20:17Z, one sweep after merge, on THIS PR (#10742) — the cheap observation predicted above, taken rather than deferred. items.title: A better explanation for the never-traded legs than 'long-horizon'
items.blocked_on: operator — the remedy is a Tier-3 disposition or a netted-symbol arbitration policy
items.note: ⚠️ MORNING REPORT. Found by backlog drain #3 (session_01JXBmVC) and it LANDS ON A NUMBER PHASE G MEASURED HOURS EARLIER AND COULD NOT EXPLAIN. Phase G: 12 of 52 enabled legs have never closed a trade, only 11 of 52 would EVER be gradeable at the n>=20 floor; its candidate explanation was 'retire them, or accept they are long-horizon'. Drain #3 supplies a third and better one. === MEASURED, population stated: over a 30.9-day overlap window (2026-08-02T02:27:21Z -> 2026-09-02T00:40:22Z, 805 order packages / 508 closed trades — the window where BOTH diag tables are complete under their 1000-row cap), there were 352 unfilled decisions, ALL attributed, ZERO residual. 163 were `all_accounts_noop`, of which 106 `flip_suppressed_hold_policy` and 56 `hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative` — both DELIBERATE POLICY. Then the deciding test: 141 of 163 (86.5%) were raised while a position in that (account_id, symbol) was ALREADY OPEN, and in every named pairing THE HOLDER IS A DIFFERENT STRATEGY LEG. So a low fill rate on these legs is not lost opportunity — it is a second leg correctly denied a symbol another leg already owns. === THE SHARPEST CASE, filed as PB-20260902-MGC-TREND-1H-IS-LIVE-AND-STRUCTURALLY-CANNOT-TRADE: `mgc_trend_1h` is execution:live and enabled:true with 95 decisions, ZERO fills, ZERO closed trades since 2026-07-26. 55 of 55 of its suppressions were raised while MGC was already open on ib_paper, held ALWAYS by a sibling (ict_scalp_mgc_15m 48, mgc_pullback_1d 7) and NEVER by itself, because it has never held a position. Union-of-intervals occupancy of (ib_paper, MGC) is 73.3%. Three legs share one netted position on one account WITH NO ARBITRATION BEYOND FIRST-COME — which leg trades MGC is decided by arrival order rather than any policy anyone chose. === WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A DEAD LEG: a leg cannot accrue the evidence its own kill-gate demands if a sibling owns the symbol 73% of the time. The M7 gate is therefore not merely under-powered (MI-06) — it is grading legs that were never given the chance to trade. === ⚠️ TWO LIMITS I AM NOT CROSSING. (a) This is a DIFFERENT AXIS from ARBITRATION_FANOUT_MODE, which arbitrates one symbol across ACCOUNTS; this is contention among legs on the SAME account and symbol. Do not conflate them when fixing. (b) 'Structurally cannot trade' is established for mgc_trend_1h on 95 decisions with zero residual; whether it GENERALISES to the other 11 never-closed legs is UNMEASURED and must not be carried as if it were.

items.title: 17.2% of closed rows store a stop on the wrong side of entry; expectancyR reaches +206.9
items.note: ⚠️ MORNING REPORT. PB-20260821-R-AND-DOLLARS-DISAGREE-IN-SIGN was REFUSED by drain #3 rather than closed, and the refusal is the right call — its criteria split, the real-money limb PASSES (n=28, +$18.40, +44.840R, rCoverage 1.000) and the plausible-bound limb FAILS HARD. Closing on the limb that passed would be exactly the sign-flip-by-choice-of-population failure this repo has already paid for. === THE ROW GOT WORSE, and its mechanism is now proven rather than inferred: it reasoned from ONE trade (4824) that trades.stop_loss holds the CURRENT TRAILED stop rather than the initial one. Direct test over closed rows with pnl NOT NULL (n=477): 82 carry a stored stop on the WRONG SIDE OF ENTRY — impossible for an initial stop — i.e. 17.2%, against the row's n=1. Sign disagreement has spread from 2 of 31 strategy x account_class rows to 7 of 40. Worst: ict_scalp_sol_15m paper n=18, totalPnl -$2,064.01 against totalR +3,724.567. New worst expectancyR +206.920, 59x the one on file, from a SINGLE trade at R = +3,672.32. === WHY IT IS A PRIORITY RATHER THAN A TIDY-UP: it contaminates every totalR / expectancyR consumer, INCLUDING R-BASED PROMOTION GATES. A gate reading expectancyR on this data is reading a number that can exceed its true value by two orders of magnitude. === Needs its own session and the fix is Tier-3 — it changes what a promotion gate reads, which is why a drain session correctly would not write it. === Context worth carrying beside any dollar figure from this fleet: measured fleet pnlCoverage (MEASURED-only via classify_pnl) is 0.126 — 64 of 508 closed trades in that 30.9d window. 87% of the fleet's PnL is not a measurement.

items.title: The trainer relay is issue-driven, and a sub-session's issue_write is 403
items.note: MERGED as 7b95451c (#10736) — .github/workflows/trainer-diag-relay.yml, the third push-triggered relay beside pr-opener and board-post. I reviewed the WORKFLOW rather than its description, since it opens an SSH path. Findings: the SSH target is vars.TRAINER_VM_IP defaulting to the trainer's hardcoded IP and is NOT caller-controlled (the request file is the SCRIPT, not the host); permissions are contents:write only; push does not fire from forks so it is gated to accounts that could already edit any workflow and use any secret. It REJECTS the `cmd:` parser shape by citing FIVE documented truncation bugs in the existing issue relay — including one where the truncated prefix STILL RAN and returned plausible output at exit 0 — and a file has no ambient YAML, so that whole class is unreachable. Concurrency is keyed on github.sha so no request is ever dropped, citing the bug where a coarser key silently discarded a burst; that is MI-19's shape avoided by construction. ⚠️ And it describes its own scope tripwire HONESTLY as an accident guard and NOT a security boundary — 'anyone who can trigger this workflow can push, and push access already permits editing this file' — which is the framing that made me willing to merge it. ⚠️ landed_unproven: the relay has never been exercised end to end. The observation is a sub-session dropping a request and reading a result back. === ⚠️ CORRECTION TO MY OWN NOTE ABOVE, AND I PROPAGATED THE ERROR TWICE. I wrote 'the relay has never been exercised end to end' into this row AND into the sweep-8 prompt. THAT WAS FALSE WHEN WRITTEN. The author had already exercised it before I merged: trainer-diag-relay runs #2 and #3 on claude/trainer-relay-demo-scratch at 03:29:33Z and 03:30:36Z demonstrate all four states (ran / nonzero-exit / refused_empty / refused_scope) plus the name-reuse silent no-op — which is exactly what the brief demanded ('show it working, do not assert it'). I did not check the workflow's run history before declaring it unproven, which is the same not-looking this whole row is about. A successor acting on my note would have re-proved a proven thing. === ✅ AND IT IS NOW ALSO CONFIRMED FROM MAIN, POST-MERGE, BY THE MANAGER (run #5, 2026-09-02T04:25:35Z, scratch/trainer-relay-probe-0431). Result file reads state: ran · remote_exit: 0 · host ict-trainer-vm as user ubuntu. It read /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/runtime_logs/trainer/dataset_audit.jsonl — 9,352,282 bytes, 4,147 lines — which is the exact file two backlog drains were blocked on and which no /api/bot/ml/* route can serve, because publish_trainer_mirror.sh names seven files and omits it. The 4,147 INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATES the author's own figure, arrived at separately. My probe carried a negative control (a path that should not exist) and it fired: 'No such file or directory' — so the probe discriminates rather than reporting success regardless. THE CAPABILITY GAP IS CLOSED and the next drain that needs the trainer has a path.

items.title: A sub-session's 'I'll stay available' is a hand-off nothing can act on
items.note: MEASURED TWICE TONIGHT, and the second time it cost a real hand-off. The merge-train sub-session (session_01CKcZFm) ended its turn IDLE at 01:46:45Z with post_turn_summary 'staying available to re-resolve as manager merges' — an explicit offer to be re-invoked. When two of its PRs needed exactly that re-resolve, the manager tried `SendMessage` to it and got: **'No agent named session_01CKcZFm... is reachable. Use ListAgents to see everyone you can message.'** `ListAgents` lists only in-process agents and local sessions; a CCR cloud sub-session appears in NEITHER direction. === SO 'STAYING AVAILABLE' IS A DEAD END THAT READS AS A HAND-OFF. That session was holding full context on two conflicted PRs — which files, which resolution rule, what it had already tried — and NONE of it was reachable. The manager had to spawn a fresh session (session_015oCrkh) and re-supply everything it already knew. It worked, but the duplicated context is the cost, and the operator has said that cost is acceptable — which is not the same as it being invisible. === ⚠️ THIS IS THE COORDINATION LIMIT THE OPERATING-MODEL DESIGN ALREADY NAMES, observed live: 'a session that dies cannot run its own close-out', so state must be written to the WORK OBJECT as work happens rather than held in a session that expects to be woken. An IDLE session is the same case as a dead one for this purpose — the design's three mechanisms (incremental progress, a lease per session, a reaper) are the answer, and none of them is 'message it again'. === TWO THINGS A FUTURE MANAGER SHOULD DO DIFFERENTLY: (1) never write a spawn prompt that invites a session to idle and await follow-up — tell it to finish, write its state down, and stop; (2) do not read `post_turn_summary: staying available` as an owner. It is not one. The row is `queued` rather than filed to a backlog because the fix is a change to how sessions are SPAWNED and how hand-off state is RECORDED, which is operating-model work, not a bug in a file. === RE-TESTED 2026-09-02T04:15Z AND IT HOLDS, with a sharper statement. Every running sub-session's CCR record advertises `cross_session_inbound: "available"`, which reads as a capability. ListAgents from this manager returns 'No reachable agents — no other Claude session is running on this machine right now'. So the field describes a CCR-side inbound path, not this session's peer graph, and a manager reading it would conclude it can message a sub-session when it cannot. That is the same unprovenanced-output shape MI-27 and MI-36 are about, one layer up in the tooling. Practical consequence, hit tonight: #10739 needed a fix, its author was ALIVE and self-reported review_ready, and I could not tell it — I had to post a PR comment and hope it reads it.

items.title: A live alarm reads as 'never fired in 11 days' on the surface a reviewer would grade it from

items.title: The merge-ordering protocol, learned by getting it wrong three times in one night
items.note: Written into #10728 and then PROVEN under live test the same hour. The rule: resolve one → merge it → resolve the next against the NEW main. Batch-resolve-then-batch-merge cannot converge, because each merge invalidates every sibling resolve not yet landed — measured cost tonight was two wasted resolves on #10679. Under the protocol, four PRs merged in sequence with zero re-conflicts. TWO refinements learned in the doing and worth keeping: (1) a manager-only PR is the standing EXCEPTION — its conflict surface is empty, so it merges at any point in the queue without disturbing an in-flight sibling (#10728 merged while #10679 was open and #10679 stayed clean). (2) GitHub returns mergeable_state:'unknown' for up to a minute after each merge; `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/<branch>` answers immediately and authoritatively, so do not idle on the API. ⚠️ landed_unproven rather than done: it has survived one queue. It has not yet been tested against a queue containing two PRs that genuinely touch the same file.

PR #10739 — HELD BY ME, re-drafted, on a REAL CI failure I caught by checking rather than trusting. The PR reported 'PASS 50 · FAIL 0'; CI ran guards RED. Diagnosed and posted on the PR: collapsed-state-guard exits 0 with an empty FINDINGS section on origin/main and exits 1 with two findings on the branch, so the branch CAUSED it — its order_monitor.py additions now read to the guard as a db_explorer.filter_state consumer branching on ['applied'] alone. Its own two new contracts are FINE ('3 consumer(s), all states read'); the failure is a side effect. Arithmetic on the discrepancy: I get PASS 46 · FAIL 4 · SKIP 20 — the SAME skip count, so the same selection — and three of my four are my sandbox (pytest, lint-imports) which the author had installed, so the author's own run should have read PASS 49 · FAIL 1, never 50/0. Most likely the guard run predates the final commits: the run-guards-AFTER-committing trap one step along. === THE WORK ITSELF IS THE BEST OF THE BATCH and I verified its core independently: its venue reads match mine exactly, and it went further than I could — settling ownership from the journal (trade 5308, both leg ids matching, closed reconciler_filled 03:05:33Z with legs STILL RESTING 36 min later, so the legs were TRACKED not NULL), and answering my accumulation question as BOTH with the right caveat that 23 alert rows are EMISSIONS under a 6h latch and not a time series. ETHUSDT hit 20 OF 20 COMBINED LEGS on 2026-08-26 — zero headroom, the exact state where set_trading_stop refuses silently — so this is NOT cosmetic. I also checked its scope claim rather than taking it: the order_monitor.py diff REMOVES no line matching covered_qty, '>= size' or the re-arm branch; every match is an addition. === MERGED as 2c7ae605 after the author fixed its own CI failure. ⚠️ AND THE CAUSALITY IS NOT WHAT MY PR COMMENT IMPLIES — worth recording because I nearly took credit for it. The fix (5c3bf46a, 'keep the Data Explorer path out of the docstring prose') was pushed at 04:12 and its guards run went green at 04:13:56; my diagnosis comment landed at ~04:16. The session caught itself; my review was CORROBORATING, not causal. It also chose the BETTER of the two remedies I had named — it removed the prose being misread as a consumer branch rather than annotating the guard into ignoring it, which leaves the guard's detection intact instead of teaching it to skip a real pattern. I verified the fix independently rather than taking the green tick: collapsed-state-guard exits 0 on the branch. ⚠️ landed_unproven, NOT done: the per-book split has NEVER RENDERED ON THE FLEET. The observation is a bybit_over_cover row on /api/bot/logs?level=error carrying graded_book_qty and other_book_state, which needs the trader to restart on the merged sha AND the condition to recur. Merging is a deploy.

MONEY-AT-RISK, Tier-2, surfaced by #10739 and deliberately NOT fixed there — correctly, because it changes which positions get re-armed and must not ride in on a diagnostic repair. THE DEFECT: the Bybit naked-sweep's re-arm decision reads a SIDE-BLIND covered_qty. Since hedge mode was armed on bybit_1/bybit_2 on 2026-08-30, one symbol can carry legs for two books and they land in one sum — so an OTHER-BOOK leg can push covered_qty past `size` on a position whose OWN stop is gone, and `if covered + eps >= size: continue` then skips it as FULLY COVERED. Constructed on the live 2026-09-02 BTC data: had the Sell 0.018 leg been lost, covered would still read 0.46 >= 0.018 and the sweep would NOT have re-armed a naked long. ⚠️ n=1 CONSTRUCTED — no live instance of the masking has been observed, and that distinction must survive into whatever fixes it. THE FIX is to point the coverage comparison at reduces_graded_book_qty (which #10739 computes). ⚠️ DO NOT also narrow the TRIP threshold: the side-blind sum is the UNION of both conditions, so narrowing it would make the other-book case go SILENT, which is strictly worse than mislabelling it. Blocked on #10739 landing, since it supplies the per-book figure. === UNBLOCKED 2026-09-02T04:33Z: #10739 merged (2c7ae605), so reduces_graded_book_qty now exists and the fix has its input. Ready to dispatch.

TWO INSTANCES IN ONE WEEK, DIFFERENT MECHANISMS — which is what makes it a class rather than two bugs. (a) mgc_trend_1h: 95 decisions / 0 fills because a SIBLING holds MGC 73% of the time (MI-29). (b) splg_trend_long_1d, found by the performance drain (#10737): enabled, execution: live, routed, and unable to signal for 41 days — 3,660 of its 4,736 signals read 'need at least 46 candles for the donchian(30)/atr(14) windows; got 18', onset 2026-07-23T13:30:34Z, and a FLEET-WIDE sweep of the whole signals table for that message returns 3,660 rows of which EVERY ONE is that leg (run fleet-wide precisely so the negative has a denominator). === WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TWO LEGS: nothing on any config surface or /api/bot/strategies distinguishes such a leg from one that simply sees no setups. So the kill-gate is grading legs that never got to trade, and a 'no trades' reading means at least three different things — starved by a sibling, starved of candles, or genuinely no setups. ⚠️ Related but NOT the same as the accrual-clock class #10737 retired: that one is about backlog ROWS whose exit condition is vacuous; this is about STRATEGY LEGS that read live and cannot trade. The accrual guard catches the row, not the leg. Filed as PB-20260902-SPLG-TREND-LONG-1D-IS-CANDLE-STARVED-AND-CANNOT-SIGNAL.

OPERATOR-REPORTED on waking 2026-09-02, and it is the most consequential defect found tonight because it is the OVERSIGHT mechanism itself. The last message their ClaudeBot channel received was at 03:24 and read, entire: 'work_digest'. No body. === DEFECT 1, DELIVERY: work_digest.py queues its text under the key 'message'; notify_on_pull.py::_render_ping_message composes the operator-visible body from a FIXED key list that does not contain it, so the label rendered and the content was dropped. The function's own docstring promises 'nothing is silently dropped' — true of the label, false of the body, which is how the next reader stops looking. === DEFECT 2, CONTENT, AND IT IS WORSE: I ran the generator myself on the night's range and it emits 'No lifecycle change in a9444bc6..34f2beb5 (population: 584 work objects)'. That is after 52 merged PRs, the ml backlog becoming the first to clear the no-exit census, the performance drain retiring the unmeasured accrual clock, two OPEN-ITEMS rows cleared on first-hand observation, and the trainer capability gap closed. NONE of it moved a work-object `lifecycle` field, so the digest correctly reports its own metric and tells the operator nothing true. IT MEASURES THE WORK STORE, NOT THE WORK. === WHY IT RANKS ABOVE the other open items despite being small: F6 is the condition the autonomy grant rests on. A digest that fires empty is ANTI-enforcement — the operator sees a message arrive and infers they were told. Fixing delivery alone would be the worse outcome of the two available, because it would deliver a confident 'nothing happened' every night. === Dispatched with both traps named: no PR-counter (CLAUDE.md's contract is state-changes-and-decisions, NEVER activity), and 'nothing changed' must become distinguishable from 'we could not look', which today it is not.
